one_liner: Executive who runs the SEC Division of Examinations' risk-analytics and monitoring office, setting risk-based exam strategy for broker-dealers, investment advisers and other registrants.
fit_summary: This senior SEC role requires a year at GS-14 level examining or overseeing securities firms, plus a Top Secret clearance. Daniel's resume has no securities, audit or financial-regulatory work, so skip it.
eligibility: Open to the public, so U.S. citizens without federal status may apply.

Requires at least one full year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-14/SK-14: examining, auditing or reviewing broker-dealers, investment advisers, investment companies, transfer agents or SROs, or managing teams that do so.
Requires a Top Secret security clearance.
Must be in one of the listed SEC offices, with Washington, DC the nearest to Manassas; telework is not available.
strategy: Skip this one: it requires a year of GS-14-level experience examining or overseeing securities firms, and his resume has no securities, audit or financial-regulatory work.
Put his energy into emergency management and policy roles at GS-9 to GS-12 instead; good targets are FEMA, DHS, Virginia VDEM, and Prince William County or City of Manassas emergency management.
resume_bullets: Built Excel pivot-table reports on spending and order status (2021–2022).
Tracked state implementation of the Rural Health Transformation Program from November 2025.
interview_questions: Describe a time you led a team conducting examinations or reviews of securities firms. How did you set priorities based on risk?
How would you integrate risk analytics into national exam planning across program areas?
Tell us about building a coalition with external regulators or SROs during a significant market event.
How have you aligned limited resources with competing organizational priorities?
watch_outs: The specialized experience requirement for securities examination or oversight at the GS-14 level is almost certainly unmet, so you would likely be rated ineligible.
A Top Secret clearance is required.
The job is on-site only, with no telework, which would mean a daily commute to the DC office.
